It highlights the Royal Apothecary Society's grim dedication to perfecting their New Plague while despising the natural vitality of the Hillsbrad Foothills.
A Bitter Outlook in Tarren Mill

While stationed inside Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon finds little joy in the surrounding landscape. Looking out past his window at the blooming meadows and brisk mountain air of Hillsbrad, he views the region's enduring life as an offense. Like many within the Royal Apothecary Society, his personal devotion is bound to Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and the perfection of the New Plague, an engineered scourge intended to bring death to the living and retribution to their enemies.

To engineer his latest poisonous mixture, Lydon turns to the local fauna prowling the foothills and the slopes toward the Alterac Mountains. Believing that mountain lion blood possesses specific properties vital for crafting what he calls an Elixir of Pain, he sends agents into the wilds to claim ten vials. The collection serves as the foundation for the Society's ongoing chemical trials along the contested southern front.

Commissioned by Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill, this quest tasks Horde agents with testing a newly brewed biological concoction known as the Elixir of Pain. The Forsaken apothecary selects Stanley, a pet dog belonging to Farmer Ray in the Hillsbrad Fields, as an unsuspecting test subject.

Operating out of Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon conducts experiments on behalf of the Royal Apothecary Society and Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. Utilizing fresh blood gathered from the local wildlife, Lydon concocts a volatile mixture he dubs the Elixir of Pain. Rather than relying purely on theoretical alchemy, the society requires empirical field data to observe the physiological effects of their experimental poisons and mutagens.

To evaluate the draught without alarming the human defenders of Hillsbrad, Lydon directs his agents to target the northern farm in Hillsbrad Fields. There lives Stanley, a seemingly harmless pet dog kept by Farmer Ray. Approaching the unsuspecting canine with the draft poured into an open hand, the agent administers the dose under the guise of an ordinary treat.

The true nature of the Elixir of Pain manifests immediately upon ingestion. Instead of a straightforward lethal toxin, the concoction acts as a horrific mutagen, triggering instantaneous agony and violently warping Stanley's body into a savage, enraged wolf. The beast turns violently on anything nearby, proving the volatile efficacy of Lydon's alchemical formula.
